chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad, people remain in speculation until they begin speaking about Allah. So when you hear that, say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Unique, the one whom there is nothing like Him.'

key_terms.الْمُنَظَّرُ: Speculation or rational inquiry into divine attributes
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing like unto Him (divine incomparability)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on speculating about God's nature?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia theological concern with 'tashbih' (anthropomorphism) and 'tamthil' (analogy) that arise when humans project their limited understanding onto the Divine. The Imam prescribes the recitation of 'Al-Wahid Alladhi Laysa Kamithlihi Shai' as a corrective measure, grounding the believer in the concept of Tawhid al-Sifat (Unity of Attributes) to prevent deviation into speculative theology.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/371] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abi Ayyub from Muhammad b. Muslim who said:

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: O Muhammad, people keep being conversed with unless they begin talking about Allah, so when you hear that then say: ‘there is no god but Allah, the Unique, the one whom there is nothing like Him’
